newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks edge up in consolidation phase.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks edge up in consolidation phase.

text.p: Jakarta stocks edged up at the opening on Tuesday as the market underwent consolidation after making sharp gains last week, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 0.35 points, or 0.05 percent, to 700.08 points at 0315 GMT. The index was briefly at 701.59 points.

Gainers led losers by 37 to 27, with 59 counters unchanged. Total turn-over in early trade was a modest at 104 billion rupiah. "There was well-spread profit taking on the board as many counters had made strong gains recently," one broker with local firm said.
Another local broker attributed the profit taking to a technical correction after the index crossed the 700-point psychological barrier on Monday.
"The index was previously predicted to hover around 670-680 points after the polls, but now its already at the 700-point level," she said.
She said the market should consolidate in the aftermath of May 29 general election, which saw President Suharto's ruling Golkar party romping home with a landslide victory.
Brokers also said the Dow Jones' fall overnight also dampened overall local market sentiment.
Sellling interest was seen on several blue chip counters such as Bank Negara Indonesia, Bimantara Citra and Telkom and small-capitalised stocks boosted by recent speculative interest, brokers said.
Small property firm Surya Semesta was the most active stock with 10.1 million shares changing hands, but the price was unchanged price of 1,200 rupiah.

Brokers said the stock was among the target of profit takers after it made strong gains the past several days due to market talk that a foreign firm would buy a stake in Surya and on expectations of strong first quarter results.
On Tuesday, it announced a first quarter net profit of 28.28 billion rupiah against a net loss of 10.03 billion rupiah in the same period last year.
Small-capitalised garment firm Karwell rose 50 rupiah to 1,250 rupiah on a volume of around five million shares on market talk of a possible link-up with foreign company.

Adhesive producer Kapuas was active on what brokers said was due to unclear market rumours. It rose 12.66 percent to 2,225 rupiah after touching 2,325 rupiah earlier on a volume of 3.9 million shares.
